headline: GOLD $4,522 AND SILVER $68: THIRD CONSECUTIVE WEEKLY GAIN — Iran Sanctions Push Oil to $93, Warsh Keynote in 6 Days
snippet: Spot gold held at $4,522 per ounce and silver traded above $68 on Friday August 21 — both metals on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, with silver up more than 5% this week and gold posting its best August in years at +10% month-to-date. The week's driver was the U.S. Treasury's bond buyback program, which compressed long-end yields and the dollar simultaneously. Complicating the macro into Jackson Hole: Brent crude surged past $93/bbl on new U.S.-Iran sanctions pressure and a hardening Strait of Hormuz standoff — oil's advance normally raises inflation expectations and rate-hike risk, yet precious metals held their gains, suggesting a geopolitical risk premium is providing a floor independent of the rate path. Fed Chair Warsh's August 27 keynote — his first, and delivered without the forward-guidance playbook — is now the most consequential single speech for metals in years.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER PHASE 2 MINTO: 13.12% CuEq HEADLINE INTERCEPT — PEA for Yukon Restart Targets Q3 2026
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSXV: SCMI) released Phase 2 assay results from the Minto copper-gold-silver project in Yukon on August 20, headlined by infill hole 26SCM190 at Minto North returning 13.12% copper equivalent over 1.93 metres (6.01% Cu, 8.77 g/t Au, 36.6 g/t Ag) — the highest-grade single intercept of the entire Phase 2 campaign — within a broader 33-metre interval at 1.49% CuEq. Step-out hole 26SCM188 at Area 118 returned 3.73% CuEq over 6 metres within 23 metres at 1.66% CuEq. With 45,299 metres drilled in 187 holes (Phase 2 now 90% complete) and a total programme exceeding 97,000 metres, Selkirk is advancing a PEA for the proposed restart of the former Minto copper mine — an Indigenous-held past-producing asset that recently saw its resource triple to 940 million pounds. At near-record LME copper prices, a restart story this far along with drill continuity at these grades is exactly the type of pipeline asset majors are actively seeking.

headline: OSISKO METALS GASPÉ: 312m AT 0.56% Cu — Eastern North America's Largest Undeveloped Copper Hits Best Infill Width-Grade
snippet: Osisko Metals (TSX: OM) reported August 20 the latest 2026 infill drill results from the Gaspé Copper Project in Quebec — home to the largest undeveloped copper resource in eastern North America (1.834 billion tonnes at 0.27% Cu in the Measured and Indicated categories). The batch includes 35 mineralized intercepts from 15 new drill holes, with a headline interval of 312.5 metres at 0.56% Cu representing the strongest grade-width product from the programme's wide-intercept drilling to date; for context, June 2026 returned 80 metres at 1.93% Cu (high-grade zone), and July returned 320 metres at 0.38% Cu. Acquired from Glencore in 2022, the former Noranda mine targets permits and construction by the early 2030s, with an estimated US$1.8 billion initial capital requirement. Continued drill success at scale reinforces the project's position as one of the highest-conviction copper development stories in Canada — a category that commands a structural premium when LME copper is at or near all-time highs.

headline: ENERGY FUELS COMPLETES HEAVY REE TRIFECTA: Terbium Oxide Now Qualified by Japan's Largest Magnet Maker
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU) announced August 19 that its terbium oxide (Tb₄O₇) produced at the White Mesa Mill in Utah has passed all qualification tests for use in commercial rare earth permanent magnet production by the world's largest REPM manufacturer outside of China — a Japan-based firm. The same manufacturer previously qualified Energy Fuels' neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) and dysprosium (Dy) oxides; terbium qualification completes the full heavy REE commercial portfolio with no further validation required. Energy Fuels is now the only Western producer with NdPr, Dy, and Tb simultaneously approved for Japanese industrial magnet use — a supply-chain first at a moment when governments across the G7 are actively seeking alternatives to Chinese heavy rare earth flows. A commercial-scale Heavy REE separation plant is under construction at White Mesa.

headline: AMERICAN TUNGSTEN IMA MINE IDAHO: FIRST U.S. TUNGSTEN RESOURCE — 2.1M Inferred Tonnes at 0.55% WO₃, 1.8Moz Silver
snippet: American Tungsten Corp. (TSXV: TUNG) defined a maiden mineral resource estimate at the IMA Mine in northeast Idaho on August 20, positioning it as the state's highest-grade primary tungsten project with indicated resources of 316,000 tonnes at 0.55% tungsten trioxide (WO₃) containing 1,747 tonnes WO₃ and 404,000 ounces of silver, plus inferred resources of 2.1 million tonnes at 0.55% WO₃ containing 11,933 tonnes WO₃ and 1.8 million ounces of silver. China implemented export controls on tungsten in 2025; the United States currently has no operating tungsten mine of scale. IMA represents the most significant tangible step toward domestic tungsten supply in years, at a past-producing Idaho district with established mining infrastructure. Surface and underground drilling are ongoing, with a PEA advancement planned.

headline: BRENT AT $93: US-IRAN SANCTIONS PUSH AND HORMUZ STANDOFF ADD INFLATION COMPLEXITY INTO GOLD'S JACKSON HOLE WEEK
snippet: Brent crude surged past $93 per barrel on Friday, on pace for a 5%+ weekly advance, as the United States moved toward sweeping new economic sanctions on Iran while the Strait of Hormuz standoff entered another week without resolution: Tehran is demanding the U.S. lift its oil export blockade as a precondition for reopening the strait, while Washington is hardening its position. For mining investors, the oil surge injects a genuine complication into the Jackson Hole setup: rising crude lifts inflation expectations, which raises real-rate pressure, which is the mechanical headwind gold has been fighting all year. Gold held at $4,522 this week despite the oil bid — suggesting either the geopolitical risk premium is overwhelmingly the dominant factor, or the market expects a Hormuz resolution that restores the oil-as-tailwind narrative before the September 16 FOMC decision.

headline: COPPER MINERS CRUSH GOLD IN AUGUST: GLENCORE +41%, SOUTH32 +39% — Copper Sector Adds $246B vs. Gold's $18B Year-to-Date
snippet: While gold's 10% August surge has captured the narrative, the real market-cap creation in mining has been in copper and base metals: Glencore is up 40.9% in August, South32 up 39.3%, and Southern Copper up 37.9%, as copper and diversified mining companies have collectively added an estimated $246 billion in market capitalization year-to-date (+24%), compared to gold, silver, and royalty companies which have added approximately $18 billion (+2.6%). The divergence reflects the market's structural pricing of long-duration copper supply deficits — mine supply constrained, LME inventory still historically low post-August squeeze — while gold miners are only now beginning to attract capital via this week's GDX/GDXJ breakout. For junior allocation, the split is significant: base-metal juniors carry a structural bid from producers starved of new copper resources, while gold juniors are in the early innings of institutional re-rating after months of underperformance.

headline: FORTESCUE FY26: RECORD 201Mt IRON ORE, $3.2B FREE CASH FLOW — Major Miner Profitability Sets the M&A Stage
snippet: Fortescue (ASX: FMG) reported FY26 underlying net profit of US$3.5 billion (up 3%), revenue of US$17 billion (up 9%), and free cash flow of US$3.2 billion (up 25%) after US$3.6 billion in capital expenditure, with EBITDA of US$8.6 billion at a 51% margin on record shipments of 201.3 million tonnes of iron ore. While iron ore sits outside the junior mining investor's core universe, Fortescue's results are a leading indicator for the M&A cycle: senior producers generating record free cash flows at record commodity prices have both the balance sheet and the strategic imperative to acquire pipeline ounces and pounds before the next supply gap hits. Combined with Glencore, Anglo, and Rio Tinto signalling openness to deals despite increased regulatory scrutiny, FY26 profitability data underlines why the window for junior asset acquisition — particularly copper and critical minerals — remains structurally open.
